_metadata.purpose: Everyday-equivalent conversion factors. Watt-hours mean nothing to most people; phone charges, kettles, showers, and car meters do.

sources.phone_charge_wh: Typical flagship smartphone battery 12–19 Wh (iPhone 15 Pro ~13 Wh, Galaxy S24 ~15 Wh) incl. charging losses
sources.laptop_w: Average laptop in active use, ~50 W
sources.streaming_wh_per_min: IEA (2020, updated): ~0.077 kWh per hour of TV streaming incl. device + network ≈ 1.3 Wh/min
sources.kettle_boil_wh: Boiling 1 L from 15°C: ~0.1 kWh theoretical + losses ≈ 110 Wh
sources.car_g_per_km: Average new passenger car tailpipe CO2 ~170 g/km (EU/US fleet averages 2023-2024)
sources.breath_g_per_min: Human at rest exhales ~0.7 g CO2 per minute (~1 kg/day)
sources.tree_g_per_hour: Mature tree absorbs ~21 kg CO2/year ≈ 2.4 g/hour (often-cited forestry average)
sources.email_g: Short email incl. network and device share, ~0.3 g CO2e (order-of-magnitude, Berners-Lee 2020 updated)
